mascot: Bolt the Beaver — a busy beaver builder who builds sentence bridges plank by plank, word by word, always in the right order.

slides.title: Build It Right! 🌉
slides.text: A sentence is a bridge of words. Every plank (word) must be in the right place, or the bridge wobbles! 'Ravi eats a mango' — strong bridge!
slides.spoken: A sentence is a bridge of words — every word in the right place!

slides.title: Who + Does What 🧱
slides.text: A good sentence has a who (subject) and a does-what (verb): 'The cat sleeps.' Who? The cat. Does what? Sleeps. Complete!
slides.spoken: A sentence needs a who and a does-what: 'The cat sleeps.'

slides.title: Word Order Matters 🔢
slides.text: 'Ravi eats a mango' is right. 'Eats Ravi a mango' is wobbly! In English, the who usually comes first, then the does-what.
slides.spoken: The who comes first, then the does-what: Ravi eats a mango!

slides.title: Telling and Asking 💬
slides.text: Telling sentences share: 'We won the match.' Asking sentences wonder: 'What is your name?' Both need capitals and end marks!
slides.spoken: Telling sentences share. Asking sentences wonder. Both need capitals and end marks!

slides.title: Check Before You Finish ✅
slides.text: Great builders check their bridges: Capital letter at the start? Full stop at the end? Words in order? Perfect — well built!
slides.spoken: Check your sentence: capital at the start, full stop at the end, words in order!

challenges.question: Which group of words is a complete sentence?
challenges.answer: The children play in the park.
options: The children play in the park.
challenges.hint: A complete sentence tells a whole thought: who AND what they do!
challenges.misconception: 'The children play in the park.' is complete — who (children) and what (play). The others are only fragments!

options: The children play in the park.

challenges.question: Drag the words to build the sentence: 'The cat sleeps.'
challenges.hint: First comes The, then cat, then sleeps!
challenges.misconception: 'The cat sleeps.' — The first, cat second, sleeps last!

challenges.question: Which sentence has the right word order?
challenges.hint: The who comes first, then what he does!
challenges.misconception: 'Ravi eats a mango.' has the right order: who (Ravi), then does-what (eats).

challenges.question: Which sentence asks a question?
challenges.hint: One of these sentences wants an answer back!
challenges.misconception: 'Have you seen my pencil?' asks something and needs an answer!

challenges.question: Fill the blank: 'I like apples and ___ like bananas.'
challenges.hint: The second part also needs the doer word: who likes bananas?
challenges.misconception: 'I like apples and I like bananas.' — the doer word I is right! Me and my do not fit as the doer.

challenges.question: Drag each sentence! Is it a telling sentence or a question?
challenges.hint: 'The sky is blue' and 'We won the match' tell. 'Where are you going' and 'What is your name' ask!
challenges.misconception: 'The sky is blue' and 'We won the match' tell something. 'Where are you going' and 'What is your name' ask questions!

challenges.question: Fill the blank: 'The birds are flying in ___ sky.'
challenges.hint: We both know WHICH sky — the one right above us! That needs a special little word.
challenges.misconception: 'The birds are flying in the sky.' — we use the for the one sky we all share, not a or an!

challenges.question: Which sentence is written correctly?
challenges.hint: Capital at the start, capital for the day name, full stop at the end!
challenges.misconception: 'We play cricket on Sunday.' is correct: capital W, capital S for Sunday, and a full stop!
